title: Oral health practitioner
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Performing a range of oral health preventive procedures which involve working in a patient's mouth.
entryRequirements: <p style="box-sizing: inherit; margin: 0 0 16px; padding: 0; border: 0; font-variant-numeric: inherit; font-variant-east-asian: inherit; font-variant-alternates: inherit; font-variant-position: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.33333; font-family: " open="" sans",="" arial,="" sans-serif;="" font-size-adjust:="" inherit;="" font-kerning:="" font-feature-settings:="" font-language-override:="" vertical-align:="" baseline;="" background-color:="" rgba(255,="" 255,="" 1)"="">To become an Oral Health Practitioner, you must already be a dental nurse or other appropriate registered dental care professional with the General Dental Council.</p>

knowledges.detail: Regulatory frameworks, legislation, standards and codes of practice applicable to the scope of own role.
Dental and oral anatomy and physiology and their application to patient management.
Effect of disease on the range of normal human structures and function.
Use of blood sugar levels and blood pressure as indicators of health and ill-health.
Link between diet, nutrition and hydration with systemic and oral health.
Health inequalities, current policies and how these impact on health and wellbeing at an individual and population level.
How communication can support health messages and build rapport with an individual.
How an individual can be supported to make a lifestyle or health behaviour change.
Behaviour change models, their impact and use to support health behaviour change conversations.
How to support, record and review an individual with a lifestyle or behaviour change implementation plan.
How the NHS Health Check uses key indicators to assess an individual’s health risk.
Procedures for carrying out an NHS Health Check applying the national programme standards.
Procedures used in oral health clinical practice.
Importance, procedures and planning for clinical practice sessions including managing infection control, medical emergencies and referrals in various settings.
How techniques can be adapted to suit the needs of different patient groups.
Relationship between general health systems and oral health.
Purpose of general health screening activities and key health messages relating to oral health education.
Different needs and requirements of different patient groups.
Preventative strategies and how to plan for preventative practice sessions.
The importance of feedback, evidence and reflective practice to the role.
The importance of equality, diversity and inclusion in the workplace.
How to support sustainability within the workplace.

behaviours.detail: Compassionate professional behaviour and professional responsibilities making sure the fundamental needs of patients and carers are addressed.
Act with integrity, be polite, considerate, trustworthy, conscientious and honest.
Be open and honest in their interactions with patients, carers, colleagues and employers when things go wrong, known as the professional duty of candour.
Respect patients’ wishes about whether they wish to participate in the education of learners.
Willingness to learn, and be proactive in progressing in your own development.

skills.detail: Use communication to support health messages and build rapport with an individual.
Engage with individuals to make a lifestyle of health behaviour change.
Use behaviour change models to support health behaviour change conversations.
Carry out development of an implementation plan and reviews with individuals.
Carry out dental bacterial plaque indices and food debris scores.
Take dental impressions and or intra oral scans.
Carry out planning for clinical practice sessions.
Prepare clinical equipment and records for clinical practice sessions.
Carry out procedures for prevention of infection in various settings.
Carry out adaptations to procedures according to patient group.
Carry out general health screening activities.
Deliver oral health education messages to patient groups or individuals.
Deliver general systemic advice to patient groups or individuals.
Carry out planning for preventative practice sessions.
Use self reflection and feedback to improve areas of personal performance.
Identify, organise and use resources to complete tasks, applying the concepts of resource efficiency in the workplace.

duties.dutyDetail: Professional, ethical and legal requirements to ensure safe and effective oral health care.
Anatomy, physiology and nutrition to assess oral health needs.
Conduct individual reviews applying behaviour change models to promote oral health improvement.
NHS Health Checks to support individuals in understanding and managing their health risks.
Carry out procedures for oral health clinical practice.
Preventative practice to maintain and improve oral health.
Professional practice in oral health care.
